On vtx-az-055 and vtx-az+065 the stem (segment 79023, site stem_backfill) leaves the star on the OPPOSITE side from every blob, and the orange axis arrow on shw79023-az-055 points away from the shower's entire body. MARKS: the seed stem 79023 marked OUT (it is on the far side of the vertex from the whole body, 131-146 deg from every member, and it is what sets the reversed axis); the far group 82063 + 81062 + 69018 + 67016 marked OUT (a separate narrow 20.6 cm streak behind a 24.1 cm gap). Shower 80055 (198.9 MeV) by contrast looks correct: 10 members over 0-49.3 cm within 22.7 deg, compact and contiguous, start on the vertex side of its blob, detached 26.7 cm from the star -- photon-like and I found nothing to add or remove. Vertex judged first and NOT called bad: only a 7.7 cm stub touches the star, but all three blobs sit 26-30 cm from it in different directions, which is what a common origin looks like; I would rather report the shower defect than blame the vertex. Scope: 2 of 9 showers in scope (79023, 80055); the other seven (68017 2.6, 30010 2.5, 64013 1.5, 71020 1.4, 63012 1.0, 65014 0.7, 62011 0.4 MeV) are all under 3 MeV, skipped by the 20 MeV rule, not examined. The pairing that would be worth pricing is 80055 (detached 26.7 cm) against the cluster-19 blob (detached 27.9 cm) -- two detached EM blobs on opposite sides of the star -- but the display prices whole showers, not sub-pieces of one, so I could not compute it and I propose no stored pairing.
